children.description: An operating system is a software that manages computer hardware resources and provides common services to computer programs.
An operating system performs various functions such as process control, memory management, and file management.
The process of creating a new process including creating a new process control block and allocating resources.
techniques to coordinate the activities of multiple processes such as semaphores, monitors, and locks.
Algorithms used to decide which process to execute next, such as First-Come-First-Served, Shortest-Job-First, and Priority Scheduling.
The process of saving and restoring the state of a process to switch from one process to another.
The way in which the memory is organized in a computer system, including the locations of code, data, and stacks.
The process of allocating memory to a process, including Best-Fit, Worst-Fit, and First-Fit algorithms.
A technique used to handle large virtual memory spaces by dividing it into fixed-size blocks called pages.
A data structure used to keep track of the location of pages in physical memory.
A technique used to handle large virtual memory spaces by dividing it into variable-size segments.
A data structure used to keep track of the location of segments in physical memory.
Advantages of using virtual memory include increased capacity, protection, and sharing.
Limitations of virtual memory include overhead, thrashing, and fragmentation.
A situation in which two or more processes are blocked indefinitely, each waiting for the other to release a resource.
Techniques to avoid deadlocks including resource ordering, priority inversion, and banker's algorithm.
Algorithms used to manage the requests for disk access, such as FIFO, Shortest-Seek-Time-First, and SCAN.
Mechanisms used in disk scheduling including sector-based allocation, track-based allocation, and set-based allocation.
Components of a file system including the root directory, directories, files, and the file allocation table.
Algorithms used in file systems including FAT, NTFS, and HFS.
